newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Friday, with a weak domestic A share market and the absence of new A share issues and listings reducing demand for funds, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract plunged to 2.50 percent from 13.00 percent.
Turnover fell to 7.07 million lots from 16.69 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The repo rates have been hit by smaller demand for money due to a weak A share market in the past two days and a pause in the issuing of new shares," one trader said.
Traders expect the rates to regain ground early next week, with new A share issues to resume next Wednesday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up, with the most active seven-year bond, which made its debut yesterday, rising to 99.07 yuan from 98.60 yuan.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market fell to 1.69 million lots from 2.50 million.

"Many institutions which underwrote the seven-year bond at a cost of around 100 yuan were eager to support it, pushing up the market as a whole," said one trader. "But sentiment was weak on a year-end money squeeze and after continued falls."
